_meta.indication: VONJO is indicated for the treatment of adults with intermediate or high-risk primary or secondary (post-polycythemia vera or post-essential thrombocytopenia) myelofibrosis with a platelet count below 50 x 10^9/L; approved under accelerated approval based on spleen volume reduction.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, controlled, Phase 3 trial with 1:1:1 allocation to pacritinib 400 mg QD, pacritinib 200 mg BID, or best available therapy (BAT).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with intermediate- or high-risk primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera MF, or post-essential thrombocythemia MF with thrombocytopenia (platelet count ≤100x10^9/L).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Two coprimary endpoints at Week 24: proportion of patients with ≥35% spleen volume reduction (SVR) by MRI/CT, and proportion with ≥50% reduction in Total Symptom Score (TSS).
pivotal_trials.n: 311 patients randomized 1:1:1 (pacritinib 400 mg QD n=104, pacritinib 200 mg BID n=107, BAT n=100).
pivotal_trials.result: SVR ≥35% at Week 24 (ITT Efficacy population): pacritinib 200 mg BID 16/74 (21.6%) vs BAT 2/72 (2.8%), p=0.0007. The TSS coprimary endpoint was not met: pooled pacritinib 37/149 (24.8%) vs BAT 10/72 (13.9%), p=0.08.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>20%) are diarrhea (48% vs 15%), thrombocytopenia (34% vs 23%), nausea (32% vs 11%), anemia (24% vs 15%), and peripheral edema (20% vs 15%). Most common serious adverse reactions were anemia (8% vs 3%), thrombocytopenia (6% vs 2%), cardiac failure (4% vs 3%), and pyrexia (4% vs 2%).
target_moa: Pacritinib is an orally administered inhibitor of Janus-associated kinase 2 (JAK2) that also inhibits FLT3 tyrosine kinase.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was not convened because the application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring input from outside experts.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Spleen volume reduction (SVR) of ≥35% at Week 24, a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit on the signs and symptoms of MF.

citations.quote: Pacritinib 200 mg BID has a compelling effect on SVR, a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit on the signs and symptoms of MF.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on spleen volume reduction (*see Clinical Studies (14.2)*). Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 4154-1: a randomized, controlled trial (the ongoing PACIFICA trial) to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Vonjo in adults with intermediate/high-risk MF and platelet counts <50x10^9/L.

summary.text: Pacritinib (Vonjo) received priority review and was granted accelerated approval based on spleen volume reduction, a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with the ongoing PACIFICA trial required as the confirmatory trial. The drug had Orphan Drug designation (myeloproliferative disorders) and Fast Track designation.

requirement.text: 4154-2: Conduct PBPK modeling analyses to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers on the pharmacokinetics of Vonjo 200 mg twice daily to support dosing recommendations.

citations.quote: 4154-2 Conduct physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling analyses using a revised and validated PBPK model to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers on the pharmacokinetics of Vonjo 200 mg twice daily dosed to steady state, to support appropriate dosing recommendations.

requirement.text: 4154-3: Conduct a pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction trial to evaluate the effect of Vonjo 200 mg twice daily on a cocktail of substrates for CYP3A4, CYP1A2, CYP2C19, BCRP, and P-gp transporters in adult healthy volunteers.

requirement.text: 4154-4: Conduct a dedicated pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the impact of moderate and severe hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics of Vonjo 200 mg twice daily.

citations.quote: 4154-4 Conduct a dedicated pharmacokinetic trial to evaluate the impact of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics of Vonjo following administration of Vonjo 200 mg twice daily dosed to steady state in adults with moderate (Child-Pugh B) and severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) compared to matched healthy adult subjects.
